nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Biological filtration_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What organism was studied for its potential to remove DEET from wastewater?
nodes.answer: Chlorella vulgaris was studied for its potential to remove DEET from wastewater.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Biological filtration_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What were the removal percentages of DEET by Chlorella vulgaris at different tested concentrations?
nodes.answer: Chlorella vulgaris achieved a 72% removal at 5 mg/L (T1), 35% at 10 mg/L (T2), and 15% at 25 mg/L (T3) of DEET.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Biological filtration_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What are the main objectives of the study discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main objectives are to investigate the effects of DEET on the metabolic composition and pigment levels of Chlorella vulgaris and to assess its removal capacity at varying DEET concentrations.
